sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $1.70 billion to $12.0 billion [F1][F10][F196].
The step change came in FY2020, when revenue grew 49.1% as TRIKAFTA launched in the U.S. and KAFTRIO in the EU [F5][D194][P51].

FY2024 broke the pattern: revenue still grew 11.7% [F9][D402], but operating income fell to a $233 million loss on $4.6 billion of acquired in-process R&D, $4.4 billion of it from the Alpine acquisition [F24][P11].
FY2025 recovered to a 34.8% operating margin and $3.95 billion of net income [F35][F45], though revenue growth slowed to 8.9% [D446].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO carried the window, contributing 29.5pp of FY2021 growth and 26.3pp in FY2022 [D519][D522], and still 85.9% of FY2025 revenue [D529].
In FY2025 net product revenues rose $950.5 million, or 9%, primarily due to continued growth [P3], with ALYFTREK contributing 7.6pp of the 8.9% total [D590][D446].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO itself grew only 0.7% in FY2025 [D530], and Europe contributed just 0.1pp as its growth stalled at 0.2% [D496][D495].
Operating leverage was strong: operating income grew 95.6% a year against 24.2% for revenue [F197][F196], and FY2025 incremental margin was 449.1% [D463].
Diluted EPS rose to $15.32 in FY2025 [F75] while the diluted share count was flat at 258.0 million [X137][D459], so per-share growth tracked net income.
The FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% [F35] sits above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high [D663][D662].
Cost of revenue held at 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D425] as a lower overall royalty rate for CF medicines offset other costs [P4].
SG&A was the drag, costing 1.3pp of margin as it grew 19.7% against revenue's 8.9% [D467][D456][D446].
The FY2024 margin collapse of 40.9pp [D408] came from the $4.6 billion of AIPR&D, including $4.4 billion for Alpine [P11].
Below the line, the FY2024 effective tax rate of 315.5% [D390] reflected non-deductible AIPR&D that lowered pre-tax income [P5], while FY2025's 14.9% [D433] is near the window norm.
Operating cash flow was $3.63 billion in FY2025, primarily due to income from operations of $4.2 billion [F85][P1].
Free cash flow of $3.19 billion was 26.6% of revenue [F105][D431], below the 32.8% window median [D669], and free cash flow covered net income only 0.81x [D435] against a 1.07x median [D675].
Capex rose 47.0% to $438 million, 2.09x D&A [F95][D447][D436], lifting capital intensity to 3.6% of revenue [D430].
Stock-based compensation of $686 million equalled 18.9% of operating cash flow [X87][D437], a persistent non-cash add-back.
Net cash of $12.3 billion is 102.7% of revenue [D439][D440], in the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers whose median is -50.7% [D691][D692].
Cash and investments rose 9.8% in FY2025 [D460], primarily due to increased cash and marketable securities from product revenue [P2].
Buybacks of $2.02 billion absorbed 63.2% of free cash flow [D441][D442], yet the diluted share count was unchanged [D459].
Return on average equity of 22.5% [D445] trails the 38.7% peer median [D696], reflecting the large cash balance.

Days inventory outstanding jumped 85 days to 373 in FY2025 [D444][D397], far above the 156 days of FY2022 [D298], a build that ties up cash as inventory grew 39.9% against revenue's 8.9% [D462][D446].
The effective tax rate swung -300.7pp to 14.9% in FY2025 [D433][D390], but this reverses FY2024's Alpine-driven distortion [P5] and looks benign.
FY2019 share repurchases were later restated to $186.0 million from the $192.0 million used here [X141][R3], a data-quality note that does not change any conclusion.

If TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth stays at or below the FY2025 level of 0.7% [D530] while ALYFTREK's 7.6pp contribution [D590] does not offset it, total growth would fall below the 8.9% of FY2025 [D446]; watch the product table in the FY2026 10-K.
Days inventory outstanding at 373 [D444] should be watched against the FY2022 level of 156 [D298]; a further rise would confirm the working-capital drag.
Free cash flow conversion of 0.81x [D435] against the 1.07x window median [D675] would confirm improvement if it returns above the median in the FY2026 cash flow statement.
